elements.problem: Five parts, all present in both check_for and the admission priority rule. 'Drowsy' = Drowsy (finding). 'Confused' = Acute confusion (finding): SNOMED has no plain 'Confusion' finding (closest alternatives are Clouded consciousness and Disorientated), so Acute confusion is an acceptable choice. 'Neck stiffness' = Stiff neck. 'Severe headache' = Headache + Severe (severity modifier) qualifier. 'Persistent vomiting' = Persistent vomiting (disorder).

elements.problem: 'Unable to walk unaided' means the patient needs help or an aid to walk. It is encoded as (or 'Difficulty walking' 'Unable to walk'). 'Difficulty walking' is much broader than the page (any difficulty walking makes an RR-TB patient Urgent for admission), and 'Unable to walk' is narrower. SNOMED has exact matches: 'Needs help with walking' (finding) and 'Dependent for walking' (finding), both children of 'Finding related to ability to walk'. Either should replace 'Difficulty walking'; 'Unable to walk' can stay as a stricter sibling.

elements.problem: All ten triage parts are in the second priority rule and in the check_for: RR >= 30; breathless at rest = Dyspnea at rest; breathless while talking = 'Unable to complete a sentence in one breath' (a reasonable proxy); prominent use of breathing muscles = Accessory respiratory muscles used; drowsy; confused = Acute confusion; coughs up fresh blood = Hemoptysis (the '>= 1 tablespoon' volume cannot be expressed, so plain Hemoptysis will trigger on smaller volumes, which is the safe direction); neck stiffness = Stiff neck; persistent vomiting; new weakness of arm/leg = Muscle weakness of limb + New qualifier. Urgent matches 'give urgent attention and refer'.

rule_level_problems.problem: 'Unable to walk unaided' is encoded as 'Difficulty walking' OR 'Unable to walk'. 'Difficulty walking' is broader than the page and will mark any RR-TB patient with mild gait difficulty Urgent for admission; SNOMED has the exact finding 'Needs help with walking' (and 'Dependent for walking').

rule_level_problems.rule: Check for RR-TB admission and urgent referral criteria; both priority evaluations
rule_level_problems.problem: All rules are anchored on (clinical_finding (snomed_concept "Rifampicin resistant tuberculosis" "disorder")). The page is routine care for a patient already diagnosed with RR-TB; the house standard records a known condition as (active_condition X) in a due_to (with a Known present clinical_finding form in the check_for). If the system records the RR-TB diagnosis as an active condition rather than a clinical finding, none of these rules will fire.

rule_level_problems.problem: The two priority rules overlap (RR >= 30, Drowsy, Acute confusion, Stiff neck, Persistent vomiting appear in both at the same level). Not wrong, since the page has two lists with the same Urgent conclusion, but the duplication is redundant and the split by source is the only thing that distinguishes them.

rule_level_problems.rule: Urgent: RR-TB with urgent symptoms at routine visit
rule_level_problems.problem: 'Coughs up >= 1 tablespoon fresh blood' is encoded as plain Hemoptysis; the volume threshold cannot be expressed. This over-triggers on streaky haemoptysis, which errs toward safety, but should be noted as an approximation.

summary: The red box and the Symptoms row's urgent list are both encoded as Urgent priority rules with correct thresholds and existing SNOMED concepts, but two red-box admission criteria are missing outright ('Infection control challenges at home' and 'Unstable social circumstances', both encodable), and 'Unable to walk unaided' is widened to 'Difficulty walking' when SNOMED has 'Needs help with walking'. Every rule is anchored on a clinical_finding of the RR-TB disorder rather than an active_condition, which may stop the rules firing for a diagnosed patient. Hb < 8 is correctly left out as unrepresentable; the check_for list is fully consumed by the priority rules.
